sections.heading: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojna (PM-AJAY)
sections.html:
PM-AJAY is a flagship scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment dedicated to the socio-economic empowerment of Scheduled Castes. The scheme promotes livelihood opportunities, strengthens village infrastructure, and enhances access to education and residential facilities for sustainable and inclusive development.

New Delhi

Headquarters

sections.heading: About the Scheme
sections.html:
Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) is a scheme of the Government of India, implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, for the integrated socio-economic development of Scheduled Castes across the country.

PM-AJAY works towards:

  • Reducing poverty among Scheduled Caste communities by creating employment opportunities through skill development and income-generating initiatives.
  • Improving socio-economic indicators by ensuring adequate infrastructure and essential services in Scheduled Caste dominated villages.
  • Increasing literacy and encouraging enrolment of Scheduled Castes in schools and higher education institutions, including through residential facilities.

The scheme has the components –

  1. Adarsh Gram: Develops Scheduled Caste dominated villages into model villages;
  2. Grants-in-Aid: Livelihood, Skilling, and Infrastructure projects for the economic betterment of Scheduled Castes;
  3. Hostels: supports the construction and repair of hostels for Scheduled Caste students to reduce dropout rates.

sections.heading: PRADHAN MANTRI ANUSUCHIT JAATI ABHYUDAY YOJANA (PM-AJAY)
1. Introduction and Scope
sections.html:
This document consolidates verified narrative, objectives, design features, policy evolution and key statistical tables for the three precursor schemes merged into Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) from 2021–22, and for the unified scheme thereafter. Sources are the Annual Reports of the Department of Social Justice & Empowerment for 2007–08 to 2025–26.

The three constituent streams are:

  • Special Central Assistance to Scheduled Caste Sub Plan (SCA to SCSP) — later the Grants-in-Aid (GIA) component of PM-AJAY;
  • Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMAGY) — later the Adarsh Gram component of PM-AJAY; and
  • Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana (BJRCY) — later the Hostel component of PM-AJAY.

Detailed annexure-level state-wise tables are maintained in the companion Excel file PM_AJAY_Historical_Statistical_Compendium_2007-26.xlsx and in year-wise extraction workbooks. This document embeds the principal all-India and selected state-wise series.

2. Special Central Assistance to Scheduled Caste Sub Plan (SCA to SCSP)

2.1 Origin and mandate

The Special Component Plan (SCP) for Scheduled Castes, later renamed the Scheduled Castes Sub Plan (SCSP), was introduced in 1979–80 to channelise plan outlays for SC development in proportion to SC population (16.2 per cent as per Census 2001). Special Central Assistance (SCA) to SCSP is a Central Sector scheme providing additional support to States and UTs for economic development of Scheduled Castes, including composite income-generating schemes and, within ceilings, infrastructure in SC-dominated villages.

2.2 Design features

  • Up to 10 per cent of the total release to a State/UT may be used for infrastructure in villages with 50 per cent or more SC population;
  • At least 15 per cent of SCA is to be utilised for SC women;
  • State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations (SCDCs) identify beneficiaries, arrange margin money and subsidy, and dovetail with NSFDC/bank credit.

2.5 Transition into the GIA component of PM-AJAY

From 2021–22, SCA to SCSP was subsumed as the Grants-in-Aid (GIA) component of PM-AJAY. Project Appraisal cum Convergence Committees (PACC) consider multi-year perspective plans of States/UTs.

3. Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMAGY)

3.1 Launch and pilot design

PMAGY was approved as a Centrally Sponsored pilot for integrated development of about 1,000 villages with more than 50 per cent SC population. The pilot was launched in March 2010. There were 44,080 such villages across 25 States and 2 UTs. Five States representing five regions were selected for the pilot:

3.3 Vision of an Adarsh Gram and monitorable indicators

An Adarsh Gram is a village in which people have access to basic services so that minimum needs of all sections are met and disparities are reduced. After merger into PM-AJAY, about 50 socio-economic monitorable indicators are tracked under 10 domains: drinking water and sanitation; education; health and nutrition; social security; rural roads and housing; electricity and clean fuel; agricultural practices; financial inclusion; digitisation; and livelihood and skill development.

Declaration requires the village to be Open Defecation Free (ODF) and to achieve a score of 70 or above. Proposals move from the District-level PACC to the State Government and are published on the scheme portal. Up to 50 per cent of scheme funds allocated to States/UTs may be used for gap-filling in selected villages.

4. Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana (BJRCY)

4.1 Objective and funding pattern

BJRCY provides hostel facilities to SC boys and girls in middle schools, higher secondary schools, colleges and universities. State Governments, UT Administrations, and Central and State Universities are eligible for central assistance for new construction and expansion; NGOs and private deemed universities only for expansion.

Illustrative pre-merger cost-sharing (AR 2010–11): State Governments — Boys 50:50 Central:State, Girls 100 per cent Central; UTs — 100 per cent Central for both; Central Universities — Boys 90:10, Girls 100 per cent Central. A one-time grant (₹2,500 per student in earlier years; ₹5,000 under PM-AJAY) covers cot, table, chair and common facilities.

4.3 Hostel component under PM-AJAY

From 2021–22, BJRCY is the Hostel component of PM-AJAY. Priority is given to hostels in NIRF top-ranked higher educational institutions funded by the Centre/State/UT, and in schools recommended by the Ministry of Education. Up to about 2 per cent of scheme funds may go to central institutions. Cost norms (AR 2022–23): North-Eastern Region ₹3.50 lakh per inmate; Northern Himalayan Region ₹3.25 lakh; Gangetic Plains and Lower Himalayan Region ₹3.00 lakh; one-time grant ₹5,000 per student. Assistance is released in two equal instalments.

5. Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) — Unified Scheme

5.1 Vision and three components

PM-AJAY, implemented from 2021–22, merges PMAGY, SCA to SCSP and BJRCY. Its vision is to reduce poverty among SC communities through skill development, income-generating schemes and related initiatives, and to improve socio-economic indicators by ensuring adequate infrastructure and services in SC-dominated villages. The three components are: (a) Adarsh Gram; (b) Grants-in-Aid for district/State projects; (c) Hostels.

The scheme is 100 per cent Central funded. Component orientation: Adarsh Gram up to 50 per cent of allocated funds for gap-filling; Administration up to 5 per cent; Hostels up to about 2 per cent for central institutions; balance for GIA projects, allocated with reference to SC population and State SCSP ratio.

6. Cross-cutting Themes

6.1 Convergence

From the PMAGY pilot onwards, and more explicitly under PM-AJAY, Reports emphasise convergence of Central and State schemes so that gap-filling remains residual. States are expected to mobilise three to four times the gap-filling outlay through other schemes.

6.2 Gender focus

SCA guidelines required a minimum share for SC women. BJRCY provided more favourable central funding for girls’ hostels (often 100 per cent Central). Under PM-AJAY, residential facilities and livelihood projects continue to be framed as equity instruments within the SC population.

6.3 Monitoring and transparency

Portal-based publication of Adarsh Gram declarations, milestone-based release conditions, social audit, evaluation and district-level awards are features of the post-2021 design. Pre-merger reports relied more on utilisation certificates and State-wise annexures printed in the Annual Report.

sections.heading: Organisational Set-Up
sections.html:
The Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment is entrusted with the welfare, social Justice and empowerment of disadvantaged and marginalized section of the society viz. Scheduled Caste, Backward Classes, Persons with Disabilities, Senior Citizens, and Victims of Drug Abuse etc.

Basic objective of the policies, programmes, law and institution of the Indian welfare system is to bring the target groups into the mainstream of development by making them self-reliant.

The Ministry is headed by　Dr. Virendra Kumar, Cabinet Minister and ably assisted by two Ministers-of-State namely Shri Ramdas Athawale and Shri B L Verma.

sections.heading: Hostels
sections.html:
The Hostels component of PM-AJAY supports the construction and repair of hostels for Scheduled Caste students, with the objective of containing and reducing dropout rates, particularly among Scheduled Caste girls. These hostels provide safe and reliable residential facilities to students from rural and remote areas, enabling them to pursue quality education without disruption.

Central assistance under this component is available to higher educational institutions ranked among the top institutions under the National Institutional Ranking Framework, other Central Institutes, and State institutions and schools that are fully or partially funded by Central or State Governments. Funding covers the construction of new hostel buildings as well as the repair of existing hostels, including those built under the earlier Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana.

A one-time grant is also provided for essential furnishings and common facilities in newly constructed hostels. Institutions receiving support are required to reserve 70% of hostel seats for Scheduled Caste students, and girls’ hostels are required to have lady wardens and guards available at all times, ensuring safe and supportive living conditions for all residents.

title: Development of SC dominated villages into “Adarsh Gram”

sections.heading: Adarsh Gram
sections.html:
The Adarsh Gram component of PM-AJAY works towards the integrated development of Scheduled Caste dominated villages, that is, villages with a Scheduled Caste population of more than 40% and a total population of 500 or more. The objective is to ensure that everyone in the Adarsh Gram village have access to the basic infrastructure and services necessary for a dignified life, thereby reducing disparities between Scheduled Castes and the rest of the population.

Progress under this component is measured against 50 monitorable indicators across 10 domains, covering drinking water and sanitation, education, health and nutrition, social security, rural roads and housing, electricity and clean fuel, agricultural practices, financial inclusion, digitisation, and livelihood and skill development. A Village Development Plan is prepared for each selected village, identifying gaps that cannot be met through convergence with other Central and State schemes. These gaps are addressed through dedicated “Gap-filling” funds provided under the scheme. A village becomes eligible for declaration as an Adarsh Gram on achieving a score of 70 or above out of 100, along with Open Defecation Free status.

sections.heading: PM-AJAY Implementation Process Workflows
sections.html:
Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) operates through standardized procedural workflows across its three core components: Adarsh Gram, Grants-in-Aid, and Hostels.

1. Adarsh Gram Component Workflow

Village Selection (SC population > 40%) → Baseline Survey of 50 Indicators → Village Development Plan (VDP) Formulation → Gap-filling Fund Release → Project Execution → Declaration as Model Village upon achieving score ≥ 70.

2. Grants-in-Aid (GIA) Component Workflow

Annual Action Plan submission by State Government / UT → Project Appraisal Committee (PAC) Review → Central Approval & 1st Installment Release → Milestone Verification & Utilization Certificate (UC) → 2nd Installment Release.

3. Hostel Construction & Repair Workflow

State Proposal Submission with Land Title → Techno-Economic Appraisal → Sanction of Capital Grant → Construction / Renovation Monitoring via MIS → Completion and Student Allotment.

Interactive process diagrams can be viewed and downloaded via the PM-AJAY Flowchart Portal.

sections.heading: Grants-in-Aid
sections.html:
The Grants-in-Aid component of PM-AJAY supports Livelihood, skilling, and infrastructure related projects aimed at the economic betterment of Scheduled Castes. It gives States and Union Territories the flexibility to design projects suited to local requirements, with the objective of increasing incomes, improving socio-economic indicators, and encouraging enrolment of Scheduled Castes in education.

Projects under this component fall into three broad categories. Comprehensive Livelihood Projects support skill development, and where required, financial assistance towards the creation or acquisition of assets by beneficiaries for livelihood generation. Infrastructure Development Projects address socio-economic development needs in Scheduled Caste dominated villages, including the construction of residential schools. Special Tutoring supports educationally backward children of the target group studying in classes 9 to 12, to help improve their academic outcomes.

To ensure inclusive and balanced implementation, at least 15% of funds released to States and Union Territories are directed towards income-generating schemes for Scheduled Caste women, and at least 10% towards skill development programmes.

2.5 Transition into the GIA component of PM-AJAY

From 2021–22, SCA to SCSP was subsumed as the Grants-in-Aid (GIA) component of PM-AJAY. GIA supports comprehensive livelihood projects (income generation, skill development, infrastructure), infrastructure in SC-dominated villages including Adarsh Gram villages, and residential schools where required. Project Appraisal cum Convergence Committees (PACC) consider multi-year perspective plans of States/UTs.

3.3 Vision of an Adarsh Gram and monitorable indicators

An Adarsh Gram is a village in which people have access to basic services so that minimum needs of all sections are met and disparities are reduced. After merger into PM-AJAY, about 50 socio-economic monitorable indicators are tracked under 10 domains: drinking water and sanitation; education; health and nutrition; social security; rural roads and housing; electricity and clean fuel; agricultural practices; financial inclusion; digitisation; and livelihood and skill development.

Declaration requires the village to be Open Defecation Free (ODF) and to achieve a score of 70 or above. Proposals move from the District-level PACC to the State Government and are published on the scheme portal. Up to 50 per cent of scheme funds allocated to States/UTs may be used for gap-filling in selected villages.

4. Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana (BJRCY)

4.1 Objective and funding pattern

BJRCY provides hostel facilities to SC boys and girls in middle schools, higher secondary schools, colleges and universities. State Governments, UT Administrations, and Central and State Universities are eligible for central assistance for new construction and expansion; NGOs and private deemed universities only for expansion.

Illustrative pre-merger cost-sharing (AR 2010–11): State Governments — Boys 50:50 Central:State, Girls 100 per cent Central; UTs — 100 per cent Central for both; Central Universities — Boys 90:10, Girls 100 per cent Central. A one-time grant (₹2,500 per student in earlier years; ₹5,000 under PM-AJAY) covers cot, table, chair and common facilities.

4.3 Hostel component under PM-AJAY

From 2021–22, BJRCY is the Hostel component of PM-AJAY. Priority is given to hostels in NIRF top-ranked higher educational institutions funded by the Centre/State/UT, and in schools recommended by the Ministry of Education. Up to about 2 per cent of scheme funds may go to central institutions. Cost norms (AR 2022–23): North-Eastern Region ₹3.50 lakh per inmate; Northern Himalayan Region ₹3.25 lakh; Gangetic Plains and Lower Himalayan Region ₹3.00 lakh; one-time grant ₹5,000 per student. 5. Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) — Unified Scheme

5.1 Vision and three components

PM-AJAY, implemented from 2021–22, merges PMAGY, SCA to SCSP and BJRCY. Its vision is to reduce poverty among SC communities through skill development, income-generating schemes and related initiatives, and to improve socio-economic indicators by ensuring adequate infrastructure and services in SC-dominated villages. The three components are: (a) Adarsh Gram; (b) Grants-in-Aid for district/State projects; (c) Hostels.

The scheme is 100 per cent Central funded. Component orientation: Adarsh Gram up to 50 per cent of allocated funds for gap-filling; Administration up to 5 per cent; Hostels up to about 2 per cent for central institutions; balance for GIA projects, allocated with reference to SC population and State SCSP ratio.

6. Cross-cutting Themes

6.1 Convergence

From the PMAGY pilot onwards, and more explicitly under PM-AJAY, Reports emphasise convergence of Central and State schemes so that gap-filling remains residual. States are expected to mobilise three to four times the gap-filling outlay through other schemes.

6.2 Gender focus

SCA guidelines required a minimum share for SC women. BJRCY provided more favourable central funding for girls’ hostels (often 100 per cent Central). Under PM-AJAY, residential facilities and livelihood projects continue to be framed as equity instruments within the SC population.

6.3 Monitoring and transparency

Portal-based publication of Adarsh Gram declarations, milestone-based release conditions, social audit, evaluation and district-level awards are features of the post-2021 design. Pre-merger reports relied more on utilisation certificates and State-wise annexures printed in the Annual Report.

The Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment is entrusted with the welfare, social Justice and empowerment of disadvantaged and marginalized section of the society viz. Scheduled Caste, Backward Classes, Persons with Disabilities, Senior Citizens, and Victims of Drug Abuse etc.

sections.heading: Construction & Repair of Hostels
sections.html:
Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojna (PM-AJAY)

Construction/Repair of Hostels

Hostels

The Hostels component of PM-AJAY supports the construction and repair of hostels for Scheduled Caste students, with the objective of containing and reducing dropout rates, particularly among Scheduled Caste girls. These hostels provide safe and reliable residential facilities to students from rural and remote areas, enabling them to pursue quality education without disruption.

Central assistance under this component is available to higher educational institutions ranked among the top institutions under the National Institutional Ranking Framework, other Central Institutes, and State institutions and schools that are fully or partially funded by Central or State Governments. Funding covers the construction of new hostel buildings as well as the repair of existing hostels, including those built under the earlier Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana.

A one-time grant is also provided for essential furnishings and common facilities in newly constructed hostels. Institutions receiving support are required to reserve 70% of hostel seats for Scheduled Caste students, and girls’ hostels are required to have lady wardens and guards available at all times, ensuring safe and supportive living conditions for all residents.

title: Development of SC Dominated Villages into “Adarsh Gram”

sections.heading: Development of SC Dominated Villages into “Adarsh Gram”
sections.html:
Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojna (PM-AJAY)

Development of SC dominated villages into “Adarsh Gram”

Adarsh Gram

The Adarsh Gram component of PM-AJAY works towards the integrated development of Scheduled Caste dominated villages, that is, villages with a Scheduled Caste population of more than 40% and a total population of 500 or more. The objective is to ensure that everyone in the Adarsh Gram village have access to the basic infrastructure and services necessary for a dignified life, thereby reducing disparities between Scheduled Castes and the rest of the population.

Progress under this component is measured against 50 monitorable indicators across 10 domains, covering drinking water and sanitation, education, health and nutrition, social security, rural roads and housing, electricity and clean fuel, agricultural practices, financial inclusion, digitisation, and livelihood and skill development. A Village Development Plan is prepared for each selected village, identifying gaps that cannot be met through convergence with other Central and State schemes. These gaps are addressed through dedicated “Gap-filling” funds provided under the scheme. A village becomes eligible for declaration as an Adarsh Gram on achieving a score of 70 or above out of 100, along with Open Defecation Free status.

sections.heading: Grants-in-Aid to States & Districts
sections.html:
Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojna (PM-AJAY)

Grants-in-aid to State/Districts

Grants-in-Aid

The Grants-in-Aid component of PM-AJAY supports Livelihood, skilling, and infrastructure related projects aimed at the economic betterment of Scheduled Castes. It gives States and Union Territories the flexibility to design projects suited to local requirements, with the objective of increasing incomes, improving socio-economic indicators, and encouraging enrolment of Scheduled Castes in education.

Projects under this component fall into three broad categories. Comprehensive Livelihood Projects support skill development, and where required, financial assistance towards the creation or acquisition of assets by beneficiaries for livelihood generation. Infrastructure Development Projects address socio-economic development needs in Scheduled Caste dominated villages, including the construction of residential schools. Special Tutoring supports educationally backward children of the target group studying in classes 9 to 12, to help improve their academic outcomes.

To ensure inclusive and balanced implementation, at least 15% of funds released to States and Union Territories are directed towards income-generating schemes for Scheduled Caste women, and at least 10% towards skill development programmes.

sections.heading: PM-AJAY Implementation Process Workflows
sections.html:
Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) operates through standardized procedural workflows across its three core components: Adarsh Gram, Grants-in-Aid, and Hostels.

1. Adarsh Gram Component Workflow

Village Selection (SC population > 40%) → Baseline Survey of 50 Indicators → Village Development Plan (VDP) Formulation → Gap-filling Fund Release → Project Execution → Declaration as Model Village upon achieving score ≥ 70.

2. Grants-in-Aid (GIA) Component Workflow

Annual Action Plan submission by State Government / UT → Project Appraisal Committee (PAC) Review → Central Approval & 1st Installment Release → Milestone Verification & Utilization Certificate (UC) → 2nd Installment Release.

3. Hostel Construction & Repair Workflow

State Proposal Submission with Land Title → Techno-Economic Appraisal → Sanction of Capital Grant → Construction / Renovation Monitoring via MIS → Completion and Student Allotment.

Interactive process diagrams can be viewed and downloaded via the PM-AJAY Flowchart Portal.
